einstellungen.text: Starting today, your phone shows how many evenings you have left with your parents.
Three hundred twelve. And every morning, the number gets smaller.
On Monday, you eat in your room. Your chair stays empty. Next morning: three hundred eleven.
Your dad wants to watch the game with you. You say no. Three hundred ten.
And you think you know what waits at the end.
Then on Saturday, you cook with your mom. Pasta, way too much sauce.
On Sunday, it says: three hundred forty. The number went up.
It's not counting how long your parents will live. It's counting how *you* live.
Then you see your dad's phone. Next to Grandpa's name: eleven.
Your grandpa lives four hours away. They only call on Christmas.
You sit down next to your dad. "Call him."
In Germany, kids move out at twenty-four, on average.
So you've got about nine years left under one roof. Then evenings turn into visits.
Your dad dials. It rings and rings.
On Sunday, your grandpa sits at your table. And Dad's number jumps to fourteen.
Then your mom's phone lights up. Next to your name: three hundred forty.
She's been counting since the day you were born.
